rationale: Y's central finding (the reverted `.to_out.0.`→`.to_out.` WeightsMapper leaving SDXL naming-conflict adapters unmapped) is a remarkably precise, well-corroborated match to the ground truth's core concern (dsocek's Qwen-image naming-conflict comment, and tthakkal's reply that they removed that exact change) — a genuine recall win. But Y buries this single insight under ~7 near-duplicate restatements with garbled, incomplete citations ('?:25', '?:309'), which reads as a malfunctioning pipeline rather than a curated review and badly hurts actionability and effective precision. X is cleanly structured, prioritized, and every finding is concretely grounded with file/line/code (test duplication and the weak peft_helper stub are directly verifiable from the shown diff); its FF-layer/text-encoder findings echo the same naming-conflict theme in spirit though not the literal instance GT flagged, and its CI-failure claim is unverifiable and slightly suspect given both human reviewers LGTM'd with no CI complaints. Overall X is far more actionable and trustworthy despite Y's one sharper recall hit.
